title: Enbridge affiliate Wexpro lassoes Laramie Energy for US$485M
summary: Bolsters energy affordability for Enbridge Gas customers in Utah, Wyoming, Idaho; provides Enbridge utility return without commodity exposure
body_markdown:
Bolsters energy affordability for Enbridge Gas customers in Utah, Wyoming, Idaho; provides Enbridge utility return without commodity exposure


November 23, 2026


The Wexpro model.


Since 1981, it’s delivered **[about US$350 million in savings](https://www.enbridge.com/~/media/Enb/Documents/Investor-Relations/2026/Q3_2026_Earnings_Presentation_Final.pdf#page=8)** for Enbridge Gas customers in Utah, Wyoming and Idaho.


After lassoing Laramie Energy, **[expect much more of the same](https://www.utahmoneywatch.com/enbridges-wexpro-closes-485-million-colorado-gas-deal-and-projects-700-million-in-customer-savings-over-35-years-mostly-for-utah-clients/)** .


On Nov. 18, Wexpro—an Enbridge company—announced that **[its US$485-million acquisition](https://www.enbridge.com/media-center/news/details?id=123894&lang=en)** of Laramie Energy’s Colorado natural gas assets had been **[approved by the Public Service Commissions of Utah and Wyoming](https://www.enbridgegas.com/about-enbridge-gas/newsroom/newsdetail?releaseId=%7bCCBC5BE5-25BB-420F-A448-65DE69B31844%7d&ref=utahmoneywatch.com)** .


With about 550 producing wells based primarily in Wyoming, Wexpro currently supplies about 40% of the gas consumed by Enbridge Gas Utah, Wyoming and Idaho customers. The acquisition of these **[Laramie Energy assets](https://www.laramie-energy.com/operations/)** , located in western Colorado’s Piceance Basin, **[will significantly boost that total](https://www.utahmoneywatch.com/enbridges-wexpro-closes-485-million-colorado-gas-deal-and-projects-700-million-in-customer-savings-over-35-years-mostly-for-utah-clients/)** .


**TOP AND ABOVE PHOTOS** : With about 550 producing wells based primarily in Wyoming, Wexpro currently supplies about 40% of the gas consumed by Enbridge Gas Utah, Wyoming and Idaho customers; the acquisition of Laramie Energy assets will siginficantly boost that total.


An exploration and production company, Wexpro sources natural gas and delivers it to the utility at cost of service, rather than simply selling its production at market prices.


The arrangement protects customers of Enbridge Gas Utah, Wyoming and Idaho against commodity price volatility, providing a more stable and affordable gas supply over the long term.


“We know a warm home and hot water are essential. That’s why we continue working to keep natural gas as budget friendly as it is reliable for all our customers,” says Heidi Bredenholler-Prasad, President of Enbridge Gas Utah, Wyoming and Idaho.


“Adding a long-term natural gas source in the Rocky Mountain region to our inventory bolsters energy security and strengthens reliability while fostering greater price stability and affordability for our customers now and in the coming decades,” adds Brady Rasmussen, President of Wexpro.

The transaction, which effectively includes the acquisition of all of Laramie Energy’s assets, includes up to US$65 million in contingent payments.


The move allows Enbridge to:


- Convert producing natural gas assets into a regulated, utility-linked investment with relatively predictable returns.
- Deepen its integration across gas production, supply and distribution in the Rockies.


“The transaction leverages our existing successful Wexpro business model to provide our utility customers with a stable, cost-of-service source of natural gas, helping improve affordability and moderate commodity price volatility while **[providing us a utility return without taking on commodity exposure](https://www.enbridge.com/~/media/Enb/Documents/Investor-Relations/2026/2026_Q3_Transcript.pdf#page=6)** ,” noted Enbridge President and CEO Greg Ebel during our Q3 financials call on Nov. 6.


Including Laramie assets, Wexpro’s operations now stretch from the northern tip of the Greater Green River Basin in Pinedale, WY, down through the Vermilion Basin of Wyoming and Colorado, the Piceance Basin of Colorado, and the Uinta Basin of Utah.
